newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan phone firms to share cable in industry shift.
newsitem.headline: Japan phone firms to share cable in industry shift.

text.p: The second-largest Japanese telephone company, DDI Corp., said Friday it would use an undersea cable to be laid by a long-distance carrier in an alliance that points to a shake-up in the nation's telecommunications industry.

DDI, Japan's second biggest domestic operator behind Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp. (NTT), said it agreed to buy 20 percent of the transmission capacity of the cable, to be laid around Japan by mid-1999.

The purchase of capacity on the cable, being installed by Kokusai Denshin Denwa Co., could be the start of a fundamental realignment of Japan's huge telecom market triggered by deregulation, industry analysts said.
A DDI spokesman said the company had agreed to buy 20 percent of the capacity from KDD but had yet to pin down the details, including the cost.
"We will negotiate over specifics and would like to sign the agreement in early 1997," he said.
Japanese telephone operators have long been restricted to certain segments of the market, such as local, domestic long-distance and international operations.

But deregulation, including a restructuring of the colossal NTT, is expected to force smaller telephone operators to seek partners to strengthen their position or risk seeing their business slip away.

KDD's new cable, to be built at a cost of around $900 million, will help meet growing Japanese demand for telephone services, including surfing the Internet, and give KDD the muscle to expand into NTT's domestic territory.
The cable will loop around Japan's three main islands and carry 1.2 million telephone lines, with voice and data transmission capacity of 100 billion bites of data a second.

NTT -- currently banned from offering international services -- is expected to announce the launch of international operations through a wholly owned unit in early January as part of its restructuring.
